proposals.after: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was recalled as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, then promoted to Chamberlain of the Imperial Seal.

proposals.before: I cannot bear to watch the empire sink; I beg Your Majesty to read this memorial through, change course with the Grand Secretariat and ministry heads, and return wholly to the ancestral statutes — then even if I join the loyal dead underground, I shall count myself among the living.
proposals.after: I cannot bear to watch the empire sink; I beg Your Majesty to read this memorial through, change course with the Grand Secretariat and ministry heads, and return wholly to the ancestral statutes — then even if I follow Peng and Gan underground, I shall count myself among the living.
proposals.reason: 逢 and 幹 are named exemplars; the idiomatic rendering drops the personal names.

proposals.before: Finally, in autumn of the forty-first year, as the empress dowager's birthday approached, at the request of Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao, he was released together with Wang Bangcai and Bian Kongshi.
proposals.after: Finally, in autumn of the forty-first year, as the imperial longevity festival approached, at the request of Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao, he was released together with Wang Bangcai and Bian Kongshi.

proposals.before: After Shenyang fell many officials looked to Xiong Tingbi to save Liaodong, but Supervising Secretary Guo Gong alone blamed Tingbi for losing the army and asked that Grand Secretary Liu Yijing be punished as well.
proposals.after: After Shenyang fell, many court officials thought of Xiong Tingbi, but Supervising Secretary Guo Gong alone blamed Tingbi for losing the army and misleading the state, and asked that Grand Secretary Liu Yijing be punished as well.
proposals.reason: Chinese 朝士多思熊廷弼 means they thought of Tingbi; the idiomatic line invents saving Liaodong.

proposals.before: The deadlock was not over strategy itself—whether to attack or hold—but over the feud between the frontier commanders, the circuit intendant and the grand coordinator.
proposals.after: It was not that opinions on fighting and defending disagreed, but that the opinions of those who sided with the commissioner or the coordinator disagreed.
proposals.reason: 左右經、撫者 are partisans of commissioner and coordinator, not a circuit intendant plus the grand coordinator.

proposals.before: By the time the court began deliberating Xiong Tingbi's dismissal, Wang Huazhen had already fled and surrendered Guangning.
proposals.after: By the time the court began deliberating Xiong Tingbi's dismissal, Wang Huazhen had already abandoned Guangning and fled.
proposals.reason: 棄廣寧遁 is abandoning Guangning and fleeing, not surrendering it.

proposals.before: Zhou Bingqian's outrage only deepened. Geng Ruqi of the Bureau of Military Appointments had sided with Zhang Heming, abetted Wang Huazhen, and helped oust Xiong Tingbi—directly contributing to the loss of the borderlands—so Bingqian hammered them in memorial after memorial.
proposals.after: Bingqian's outrage only deepened. Because Geng Ruqi, Director of the Bureau of Military Appointments, had echoed Heming and vigorously aided Huazhen in driving out Tingbi, causing the loss of the frontier, he submitted successive memorials attacking them.
proposals.reason: The biography subject is 秉謙 (Jiang Bingqian), not Zhou Bingqian.

proposals.before: He invoked the precedent of the Jiajing Emperor's execution of Ding Ruao and demanded that Zhang Heming be swiftly tried and punished.
proposals.after: He invoked the precedent of Emperor Shizong's execution of Ding Rukui and demanded that Zhang Heming be swiftly brought to justice.
proposals.reason: 丁汝夔 is Ding Rukui; Ruao misreads the name, and the source titles the ruler 世宗.

proposals.before: Emperor He favored Wang Sheng and thereby unleashed Jiang Jing and Li Run; Emperor Ling indulged Zhao Yao and thus brought on the disaster of Cao Jie and Huangfu Gui.
proposals.after: When Wang Sheng was favored, she fanned the treachery of Jiang Jing and Li Run; when Zhao Yao was favored, she brought about the calamity of Cao Jie and Huangfu.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names neither emperor and does not specify Huangfu Gui.

proposals.before: At the petition of his son, Director Zhu Zeng, he was posthumously ennobled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
proposals.after: At the petition of his son, Director Tongzeng, he was posthumously granted the office of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
proposals.reason: Chinese 峒曾 is Tongzeng, not Zhu Zeng; 赠太常少卿 is a posthumous office, not an ennoblement.

proposals.before: At the request of his son, the Director Zhu Zeng, he was specially granted the post of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
proposals.after: At the request of his son, the Director Tongzeng, he was specially granted the post of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
proposals.reason: Chinese 主事峒曾 names Director Tongzeng; Zhu Zeng mistranslates 峒曾.

proposals.before: Grand Secretaries Liu Yizao, Minister Zhou Jiamo, and others submitted successive memorials pleading for them, but none was accepted.

proposals.reason: Chinese 張柬之、桓彥範等五人 means Zhang, Huan, and companions as a group of five, not five additional men.
